Learning Objectives 
Module 1-1: What makes a cell living?
• Summarize the critical components of cell theory.
• List or recognize the characteristics that define cells as the smallest unit of life.
• Explore cellular diversity including:
• Recognize and describe the diversity in cell size within bacteria and 
eukaryotes and between bacteria and eukaryotes.
• Distinguish between unicellular organisms and cells that make up multicellular 
organisms.
• Recognize and provide examples of the diversity of cell types within 
multicellular organisms and across the tree of life.
• Identify and recognize similarities and differences in organization of genetic 
material in bacteria and eukaryotes.
• Recognize and describe the general chromosomal structure, location(s) (and 
sizes) of the genomes in bacterial cells versus eukaryotic cells (including 
mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes).

• Using your knowledge of basic cell organization and subcellular structures,
compare and contrast the structure and organization of bacterial and eukaryotic 
cells. To do this you will need to be able to:
• Recognize and describe the evidence supporting the endosymbiotic theory of 
the origins of mitochondria and chloroplasts in the evolution of eukaryotic cells.
• Be able to interpret or make figures or diagrams of cells including:
• Identifying or diagram the major subcellular structures and compartments 
in bacterial and eukaryotic cells.
• Using a scale bar to estimate the size of objects or structures in a figure.
• Identify and recognize the major structures that comprise eukaryotic cells 
(organelles and cytoskeleton) and their basic functions.
• Define the terms genome, chromosome and gene in terms of the DNA in the cell.
